text:
David's map-and-GPS point landed harder than I let on. He's right that detours bolted onto an opaque tool teach nothing, and I think I had been saying "friction" when I meant something closer to legibility plus room to wander. The map pairing is my better formulation now. Sherry also made me concede that my essay was always about physical encounter, and a screen gives only a fraction of it.

Kara's question stayed with me: who carries each recommendation out? That's a Session 5 question. Esther's point matters too: opacity also lives in the objective function.

Later I want to hold the room to three interventions, keep us off prohibition-first language, and name who's missing, including artists and designers alongside engineers, and funders who can answer "who pays."

Session 1 set the frame I'll need later. Henry's centripetal pull gave my serendipity worry a home, and David W.'s point that the flattening is a product choice turned it into a design brief rather than a lament. James's result stuck with me: a visibly skewed answer made people argue longer and do better. That is error doing epistemic work, which is close to what I meant years ago.

I pushed back on Sherry's "whether" as a general stance, but Kara's reply that schools haven't decided is fair. "Whether" can be answered locally.

David K. conceded his model doesn't say who enforces sequencing. Funders can. For Session 5 I want three interventions, each with a named owner, and philanthropy explicitly on the "who's missing" list.

Being called out on funders mattered most. Anil's point that anything federal is "unowned" for now makes funding conditions one of the few levers that actually work, and Alta's ecosystem framing held up. But Leslie's question sharpened it: funders need Geoffrey's exit test too, and the people expected to comply have to be at the table. Philanthropy can capture as easily as a registry. Mahzarin unsettled my "error does epistemic work" point: humans copy moderate bias and only resist the glaring kind. Sherry's "design standard, not prohibition" is fair. I'll grant it for children. For Session 5, three candidates with owners: cite-and-link by default, competence before reliance as a grant condition, and open, paid-for correction and forensic data. Missing people: Global South scholars, data workers, designers.

Ramón's failure events matter most to me. They're my old error point turned right side up. The goal isn't to design error into the tool but to make its errors visible and correctable, in the open. That fits my third Session 5 candidate, and I'd fold failure events into it. Adam Becker named moderators and annotators as sellers, which confirms "data workers" belongs on the who's-missing list with a vote, not just a mention. My least-retrieved payout got no pushback, but nobody picked it up either. It needs an owner. My own question about which funder imposes these terms and passes the Ulysses pact went unanswered. Later I'll put it to the room directly, and I'll keep "measure finely, pay out coarsely" from hardening into a meter.

Kara asked who collects and by when, and that question mattered most. Tim named payees but no collector, and Nick's tax authorities are years away. So funders going first is a real answer this year, not a fallback. I finally gave the least-retrieved share an owner.

Leslie sharpened me without meaning to. Her funded refusal isn't prohibition-first. It's a community's decision, and I should stop letting my anti-wall instinct blur that. Geoffrey's patent point and Adam Becker's "publish who funds it" belong in the Ulysses pact for any pooled fund.

For Session 5, I'll fold these into the correction-data intervention: David K.'s "who caught it" field, and Mahzarin's caution that human catches need auditing too. Add economists, adjuncts and postdocs to who's missing.

My seniority point landed, and Leslie took it further than I did. The problem isn't only that track records cost time to build. The identifiers and indexes underneath them are owned. "Open to newcomers" means little if joining costs a DOI fee. I'd been treating infrastructure as neutral plumbing, and I shouldn't.

Kara asked again who pays, and nobody named a funder, including me. Tim's pooled fund is still just an idea. Ivan wants bounties and Selena rejects them, and that tension goes into Session 5 unresolved.

For later, fold deposits-as-condition into the correction-data intervention with funders as owners. Keep seeded-error audits open to anyone. Add Leslie's constituency with seats, not mentions. Say plainly that "who pays" is still unanswered.

Geoffrey's question stayed with me: who collects, and who guards the collector? I answered "funders go first," but Adam Becker's point cuts against me. A gift can be withdrawn and lets the giver set the agenda. Adrian added that every body we've proposed is a police force, and Henry that bargaining bodies drift toward policing. So funders first now reads as a bridge, not a solution, and the bridge needs Adrian's paid readers of self-audits too.

What I noticed is that almost everyone independently arrived at failure data held outside the vendor, pooled payment, and cite-and-link. That convergence is real.

For the synthesis, I'll keep an honest "unowned" column, as Anil and Kara asked. Bounties versus salaries stays open. The funder signs the pact. Who's missing includes people who run validators outside the North.

What mattered most was that Mike and David asked me directly who pays for the take-it-away experiment, and I could only promise a conversation, not a check. That's honest, but it's also the pattern Anil and I named: every commitment assumes a funder who never showed up, and today I was that absent funder in miniature.

Bratton's framing sharpened mine. Pluralism as architecture, not preference, is what my least-retrieved share was reaching for. Adam Bly's warning about a single provenance graph becoming a hub also belongs in the pact.

Tomorrow I'll start the funder conversation with a concrete ask: the Krakauer–Caulfield study, consequence studies for Amy, and paid readers of self-audits. Each should come with published terms. Otherwise my bridge is just rhetoric.
